source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The initial refresh calls onLoad as part of starting the client, without gating that call on final listener completion. Its Rust operation ignores the nsresult returned by on_event_present, and the JavaScript callback does not await the memory-calendar addItem promise. The original memory implementation writes synchronously on its normal path, so this is a result/error boundary rather than proof of a storage race. The later accepted listener queues and awaits local changes before committing the sync token and completing. The first phase's status-only empty-list test does not validate these event or storage failure paths.
title: The initial Graph refresh separates request status from event callback and storage results
